pre: The named people are the attached Characters, with their own faces and clothes.
riotEnd: Dusk, with a deep cold blue sky. Colour: stone grey and near-black, with the hot pink-red of flare light and one cold blue the only strong colours. Documentary photography: slight motion blur on moving hands and flags, the highlights of the flare are blown out, and the film grain is heavy. Unretouched. Nobody looks at the camera. 16:9. Thanks.
vaultEnd: Colour: cold steel grey and near-black, with the warm yellow of the one work lamp the only strong colour. Deep shadows with no detail in them. Scuffs, fingerprints and dust on the steel. Visible 35mm film grain. Unretouched, natural skin texture. Nobody looks at the camera. There is no writing anywhere. 16:9. Thanks.
lobbyEnd: Colour: black and dark stone, with the hot pink-red glow from the street the only strong colour. Deep shadows with no detail in them, visible 35mm film grain. Unretouched. Nobody looks at the camera. There is no writing anywhere. 16:9. Thanks.

shots.body: A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 24mm lens resting on the floor inside a bank vault at night, looking back toward its door, the frame not quite level. The vault is a small plain room lined with brushed steel plate, scratched and scuffed at trolley height, with a painted concrete floor worn grey along the middle. At the far end is the doorway: a round steel vault door as thick as a man's forearm is long, swung wide open into the corridor outside, with its bolts and a spoked brass handwheel on the inner face. On the left wall is one block of twelve steel safe deposit boxes, three rows of four, each with a small brass plate worn blank. Along the right wall are bare steel shelves. A coil of orange extension cable lies on the floor in the near foreground, out of focus. There are no people. One light source only, no fill: one builder's caged work lamp standing on the floor just inside the door, low, throwing the long shadows of the shelves up the walls and across the ceiling. The corridor beyond the door is black.

Match the attached photograph br7-vault for the place: the same small steel room, the same round steel door and the same single work lamp standing on the floor. Do not copy its framing. Here the round door is shut and we are in the corridor outside it. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 24mm lens lying on the corridor floor at the foot of the closed round vault door, looking steeply up, the frame not quite level. A scatter of bright curled steel swarf and a loop of orange extension cable cut into the near foreground, out of focus. The Accountant kneels at the door, off-centre to the left, in shirt sleeves and clear safety goggles, his tie thrown over his shoulder, leaning his whole thin weight on a heavy corded hammer drill pressed against the steel, the tip of his tongue between his teeth and sweat on his forehead. The door has only one shallow bright scratch where the bit is. At the right edge of the frame stand the black trouser legs and polished shoes of a man waiting, cropped at the knee. One light source only, no fill: the caged work lamp on the floor behind him on the left, throwing his shadow and the drill's shadow huge up the face of the door.

Match the attached photograph br7-vault for the place: the same small steel room, the same round steel door and the same single work lamp standing on the floor. Do not copy its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 100mm macro lens, very close on the scratched steel face of the round vault door. A small, ordinary, worn brass door key on a loop of string sits in a small keyhole, held between the thumb and finger of a neat pale hand in a white shirt cuff and a black sleeve, sharp. Right beside it in the near foreground, out of focus, the tip of a thick drill bit rests against the steel in one shallow bright scratch ringed with swarf. One light source only, no fill: the work lamp, raking across the steel from low on the left so that every scratch throws a shadow.

Match the attached photograph br7-vault for the place: the same small steel room, the same round steel door and the same single work lamp standing on the floor. Do not copy its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 35mm lens resting on a steel shelf inside the vault, looking out at the open round doorway, the frame not quite level. The dark edge of the shelf cuts across the bottom of the frame, out of focus. The Accountant stands in the doorway, off-centre to the left and small under the huge thickness of the open door, in shirt sleeves with his safety goggles pushed up on his forehead, the heavy drill hanging from one hand on its orange cable. He looks off to the right at someone out of frame with his mouth a little open, baffled. One light source only, no fill: the work lamp on the floor beside his feet, lighting him from below and throwing his shadow up the door. The corridor behind him is black.

Match the attached photograph br7-vault for the place: the same small steel room, the same round steel door and the same single work lamp standing on the floor. Do not copy its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 85mm lens held low at the height of his waist, close, looking up at The Governor from slightly to one side. He stands just inside the round doorway, off-centre to the right, his jacket buttoned, sliding a small brass key on a loop of string into his breast pocket with two fingers, looking straight ahead past the lens with his face doing nothing at all. The thick rim of the open vault door fills the left third of the frame, out of focus. One light source only, no fill: the work lamp on the floor below him, lighting his chin and the underside of his glasses and leaving his eyes in shadow. Behind him is black.

Match the attached photograph br7-vault for the place: the same small steel room, the same round steel door and the same single work lamp standing on the floor. Do not copy its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 20mm lens lying on the floor inside the vault, looking along the floor toward the open round doorway. The steel wheels and forks of a hand pallet truck fill the near left foreground, large and out of focus, and above them rises a stack of shrink-wrapped bricks of plain paper seen edge-on, with no printing on them. In the round doorway at the far end stands a bank security guard in a peaked cap and a dark uniform jumper, a black silhouette with a mug of tea in one hand, looking in at the stack. Two men in black suits, small, push a second pallet past him into the room. One light source only, no fill: the work lamp on the floor just inside the door, behind the men, rim-lighting the shrink wrap and throwing long shadows toward the camera.

Match the attached photograph br7-vault for the place: the same small steel room, the same round steel door and the same single work lamp standing on the floor. Do not copy its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 85mm lens resting on a steel shelf, looking out through a gap between two stacks of banded paper bricks. The two stacks are dark, soft, out-of-focus shapes filling the left third and the right third of the frame, seen edge-on, with plain paper bands and no printing. In the gap, sharp, The Ex stands in his black suit with one hand resting flat on top of a stack, looking back over his shoulder toward the door with his small one-cornered smile. One light source only, no fill: the work lamp on the floor behind him, rim-lighting his silver hair and one cheek. The other side of his face is in deep shadow.

Match the attached photograph br7-vault for the place: the same small steel room, the same round steel door and the same single work lamp standing on the floor. Do not copy its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 18mm lens fixed in the top corner of the vault where two walls meet the ceiling, looking steeply down into the room. The steel shelves along both walls are now stacked full of shrink-wrapped bricks of plain paper, seen edge-on. On the floor are one emptied wooden pallet and a heap of torn shrink wrap. Three men in black suits, seen from above as heads and shoulders, pass bricks from hand to hand in a line toward the shelves. The Fixer sits on the edge of the empty pallet in the middle of the floor eating a sausage roll, his cardboard carnival mask pushed up on his forehead. One light source only, no fill: the caged work lamp on the floor by the door, so that every man throws a long shadow across the floor and up the opposite wall.

Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 24mm lens from a first-floor window above a town street, looking steeply down and along it. The wet stone window sill and a strip of pigeon spikes cut across the bottom edge of the frame, out of focus. Below, two lines of steel crowd barriers make one empty strip of wet cobbles that runs from the bottom of the frame up to the stone steps and dark doors of a columned bank at the top. A dense crowd is packed behind the barrier on the left under plain blue cloth flags, and another dense crowd behind the barrier on the right under plain red cloth flags, seen from above as woolly hats, hoods and shoulders, all turned to face each other across the empty strip. Nobody stands in the strip. One red hand flare burns on the cobbles in the strip, and its pink smoke leans one way on the wind. Two police officers in yellow jackets stand small at the barriers. One light source only, no fill: the flare, lighting the nearest faces and the wet cobbles hot pink. There is no writing anywhere.

Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 20mm lens lying on the cobbles inside a crowd, looking steeply up, the frame tilted off level. A red hand flare burns on the cobbles in the near left foreground, out of focus, and its smoke drifts across the lower third of the frame. The leg of a steel crowd barrier crosses the near right foreground. Above, two home-made cardboard placards on wooden sticks are held up by gloved hands against the sky, one on each side of the barrier, made by two different people. The placard on the left is a wide piece of brown box cardboard with a red painted border, and reads in thick dripping brush-painted capitals: "WE CAN'T AFFORD TO LIVE HERE". The placard on the right is a taller, narrower piece of white card with a blue tape border, and reads in thin neat marker-pen capitals on four short lines: "WE CAN'T AFFORD TO LIVE HERE". The bottom edge of each placard is hidden behind the hoods and woolly hats of the people holding them, seen from below and behind. Both are rain-spotted. Far behind, small, are the dark stone columns of a bank. One light source only, no fill: the flare, lighting the undersides of the placards pink. There is no other writing anywhere.

Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 20mm lens lying on the wet cobbles beside the foot of a television camera tripod, looking up, the frame tilted off level. One tripod leg and a coil of black cable cut into the near left foreground, out of focus. The Presenter stands off-centre to the right with his back to the bank, a plain stick microphone in one hand and a finger pressed to his earpiece, wearing his practised half-smile, looking at a camera lens out of frame on the left. Behind him pink smoke rolls across the dark stone columns of the bank, and the tips of plain red and plain blue cloth flags cut into the edges of the frame. The light on him is one small hard white news lamp out of frame on the left, falling off quickly, so his far cheek is dark. Behind him the only light is the pink glow of a flare.

Match the attached photograph br5-riot-look for look only: the same dusk, the same wet cobbles, the same hot pink-red flare light and smoke. Do not copy its people or its framing. A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 28mm lens from a first-floor window directly above a street, looking steeply down. The wet stone window sill cuts across the bottom edge of the frame, out of focus. Below, an empty strip of wet cobbles runs across the frame between two lines of steel crowd barriers. On the near side of the strip a man in a red scarf and a woolly hat leans far out over his barrier, and on the far side a man in a blue scarf and a flat cap leans far out over his, each seen from above as a hat, shoulders and one arm stretched right out across the gap holding a phone pointed at the other man, the two screens glowing. Between the two phones, down the middle of the strip, two men in black suits wheel a hand pallet truck stacked with shrink-wrapped bricks of plain paper, seen from above, and neither phone points at it. Packed crowds in hoods and hats stand behind both men. One light source only, no fill: a red hand flare burning on the cobbles at the left edge, its pink smoke leaning one way. There is no writing anywhere.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 20mm lens lying on the marble floor of a dark bank lobby at dusk, looking up toward the tall double front doors, the frame not quite level. The doors stand wide open on the street, where there is only slow pink-red flare smoke and a cold blue sky. In the doorway stand four men in black suits, black silhouettes, each pulling a cardboard carnival mask on elastic down over his face. In the near right foreground, out of focus, is the dark back of a uniformed bank doorman in a peaked cap, holding one door open with a white-gloved hand. A trampled paper leaflet lies on the marble near the lens. One light source only, no fill: the flare glow from the street, throwing the four men's long shadows across the marble toward the camera. The lobby walls and ceiling are black.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 85mm lens held low at the height of his chest in a dark bank corridor, very close, looking up at Mr Blue from slightly to one side, the frame tilted off level. His head and shoulders fill the right two thirds of the frame. He glares off to the left at someone out of frame, jaw pushed forward, mouth open, shouting, with sweat on his forehead and his tie pulled loose. The out-of-focus dark shoulder of another man in a black suit cuts into the near left edge of the frame. One light source only, no fill: one red alarm lamp turning on the wall behind him, rim-lighting his hair, one ear and one cheek in hard red. The rest of his face is nearly black with one small glint in the eye. Behind him the corridor is black.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 85mm lens held low at the height of his chest in a dark bank corridor, very close, looking up at Mr Red from slightly to one side, the frame tilted off level the other way. His head and shoulders fill the left two thirds of the frame. He stares off to the right at someone out of frame, eyebrows drawn up, mouth open, shouting back, wounded, his glasses catching the light. The out-of-focus dark shoulder of another man in a black suit cuts into the near right edge of the frame. One light source only, no fill: one red alarm lamp turning on the wall behind him, rim-lighting his curly hair, one ear and one cheek in hard red. The rest of his face is nearly black with red reflections in his glasses. Behind him the corridor is black.

alarmEnd: Colour: black and hard red only. Deep shadows with no detail in them, visible 35mm film grain, sweat on the skin. Unretouched, natural skin texture. Nobody looks at the camera. There is no writing anywhere. 16:9. Thanks.
